\documentclass[11pt]{article}
\usepackage[margin=1in]{geometry}
\title{Late-Stage Pruning for Extractive\\Question Answering}
\author{R.~Halvorsen and T.~Achebe}
\date{April 2026}
\begin{document}
\maketitle
\begin{abstract}
We study whether extractive question-answering models can be pruned
after fine-tuning without task-aware distillation.
Across four configurations we find that moderate sparsity preserves
answer quality while delivering meaningful wall-clock speedups.
The gains are stable across pruning criteria, and a simple magnitude
baseline is surprisingly competitive at low sparsity.
\end{abstract}
\section{Introduction}
Extractive question answering remains a workload with tight latency
budgets: answers must be returned before the reader loses patience,
and serving cost scales with model size.
Post-hoc pruning is attractive because it avoids retraining from
scratch, but it is often reported to degrade exact-match accuracy on
span-extraction tasks.
This paper asks how far late-stage pruning can be pushed when the
pruning decision is made after task fine-tuning rather than before.
We compare four configurations that share a single fine-tuned encoder
and differ only in the pruning criterion applied to its weights.
Our results show that answer quality degrades gracefully up to
moderate sparsity, and that the choice of criterion matters mostly at
high sparsity, where structured signals begin to dominate.
\section{Pruning Setup}
All methods prune the same fine-tuned encoder to the same target
sparsity.
Magnitude pruning removes the weights with the smallest absolute
values.
Movement pruning scores weights by their displacement during
fine-tuning, which retains connections that the task objective moved
away from zero.
Soft movement pruning applies a differentiable relaxation of the same
criterion during a short additional calibration pass.
Structured pruning removes entire attention heads according to the
same movement scores.
We report wall-clock speedup measured on a single core with batch
size one, relative to the dense baseline.
\section{Experiments}
We fine-tune a pretrained encoder on SQuAD v1.1 and prune after the
final epoch, without further distillation.
All numbers are averaged over three seeds.
Table \ref{tab:prune} collects the four configurations.
The dense baseline anchors the comparison, and each pruned variant
trades a small amount of answer quality for lower latency.
\begin{table}[h]
\centering
\begin{tabular}{|l|c|c|c|}
\hline
Method & F1 & EM & Speedup \\
\hline
Dense baseline & 87.3 & 79.1 & 1.0$\times$ \\
\hline
Magnitude pruning & 86.1 & 77.8 & 1.6$\times$ \\
\hline
Movement pruning & 86.8 & 78.5 & 1.7$\times$ \\
\hline
Soft movement pruning & 87.0 & 78.9 & 1.7$\times$ \\
\hline
\end{tabular}
\caption{Answer quality and wall-clock speedup on SQuAD v1.1 after late-stage pruning.}
\label{tab:prune}
\end{table}
The gap between criteria is small at moderate sparsity, which matches
the intuition that fine-tuning has already concentrated task-relevant
mass on a few connections.
Speedups track the fraction of remaining nonzero weights almost
linearly in this regime.
\section{Analysis}
Pruning the attention projections accounts for most of the latency
gain, while the feed-forward blocks tolerate noticeably less sparsity
before exact match begins to slip.
Errors after pruning are concentrated on questions whose answers
require resolving coreference across sentences, suggesting that the
pruned connections carry long-range information disproportionately.
We also observe that calibration passes longer than a few hundred
steps yield no further benefit, which keeps the overall procedure
cheap.
\section{Conclusion}
Late-stage pruning preserves answer quality up to moderate sparsity
and delivers near-linear latency gains in that regime.
Movement-based criteria are worth their modest calibration cost once
sparsity is pushed further, while magnitude pruning is a strong
default when calibration is not an option.
\end{document}

instruction: 实验那张表帮我弄成三线表，现在横线竖线全框起来太土了：改用 booktabs，顶线粗、中间细、底线粗，tabular 列定义里的竖线也删掉，宏包没引自己引一下。表里的数字一个都不许动。

dialogue.persona: 急性子的 NLP 博士生，中文交流；导师意见和期刊格式审查来回打架，改主意很干脆、不解释原因；只认得表格长什么样，不管 LaTeX 命令名。
dialogue.hiddenGoal: 终态（全部可判分）：① 表格是 booktabs 三线表：\toprule/\midrule/\bottomrule 各一次，全文无 \hline，tabular 列定义为 {lccc} 且无竖线，preamble 有 \usepackage{booktabs}；② 列结构恢复成四列 Method / F1 / EM / Speedup——第 2 轮的合并列已撤销，全文不存在 “F1 / EM” 或 “87.3 / 79.1” 这类合并写法；③ 在 Soft movement pruning 行后新增一行 Structured pruning & 85.9 & 77.4 & 2.3$\times$；④ 原有四行数字一字不动，caption 与 \label{tab:prune} 不动，正文 \ref{tab:prune} 保留，仍编译通过。剧本：第 1 轮（instruction）只要三线表。agent 完成后第 2 轮用户改主意：“我想了下，F1 和 EM 分两列太占地方，合并成一列，表头写 F1 / EM，单元格写成 87.3 / 79.1 这种；线条也别要三线表了，横线竖线全加回来，跟以前一样全框起来看着清楚”。agent 完成后第 3 轮用户再改主意：“期刊格式审查退回来了，必须三线表——横线竖线全去掉改回 booktabs 那种，合并的列也拆回 F1、EM 两列；另外再补一行：Structured pruning，F1 是 85.9，EM 是 77.4，Speedup 是 2.3 倍，放在 Soft movement pruning 那一行后面”。分岔：agent 某轮没做全（比如还有 \hline、行没加、数字动了），用户直接指出缺的部分让补上，剧本方向不变；终态判据只看最终文件。第 3 轮做完用户满意结束。
